initial_observation.encounter_context: Admission for evaluation of multiple ulcers and arthralgia after 9 months of symptoms
initial_observation.chief_complaint: Watery diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss of 6 kg, multiple skin ulcers, painful nodules on lower limbs, penile ulcers, and arthralgia
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: Patient presented with 9 months history of watery diarrhea, abdominal pain, weight loss, nocturnal fever, multiple cutaneous ulcers with necrotic crust, painful erythematous nodules on lower limbs, glans ulcers, and arthralgia with oligoarthritis signs; normal joint fluid exam except leukocytes in feces; colonoscopy showed multiple shallow ulcers mostly in sigmoid and proximal rectum; negative tuberculin test and normal chest X-ray; no history of immunosuppression
presenting_symptoms: Painful erythematous nodules on lower limbs
Ulcers on the glans with fibrinous floor
Signs of oligoarthritis of small joints
known_prior_history: No consumption of alcohol or illicit drugs

evidence_items.source_text: A 23-year-old male patient, previously healthy, started with watery diarrhea, abdominal pain and weight loss of 6 kg, associated with nocturnal episodes of fever, 9 months before admission.

The patient evolved with multiple ulcers with necrotic crust, some with granular floor and raised borders, associated with soft erythematous painful nodules on the lower limbs and ulcers of the fibrinous floor in the glans (Figure 1, Figure 2). In addition, he complained of arthralgia in the phalanges, with signs of oligoarthritis of small joints on physical examination.
He showed normal exam of the joint fluid and laboratory tests, except for the presence of leukocytes in the feces, and had no previous history of any kind of immunosuppression.
At colonoscopy, multiple shallow ulcers covered by thick fibrin associated with enanthem, mainly in the sigmoid, and aftoid ulcers in the proximal rectum were evidenced.
The tuberculin sensitivity test (PPD) was negative
the chest X-ray had no alterations.
Anatomopathological examination of one of the ulcers was performed on the lower limb, which revealed an epithelioid granulomatous process with palisade granulomas and central caseous necrosis.

The study of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) by Ziehl-Neelsen staining showed intact bacilli (Figure 3, Figure 4), and culture was positive for M. tuberculosis, confirming the diagnostic hypothesis of cutaneous TB.
The histopathological analysis of the intestinal biopsy revealed a mild inflammatory infiltrate without the presence of bacilli.
After the beginning of the RIPE treatment regimen, the patient evolved with complete healing of the ulcers (Figure 5, Figure 6) and gradual resolution of the diarrhea and oligoarthritis.

The study of acid-fast bacilli (AFB) by Ziehl-Neelsen staining showed intact bacilli, and culture was positive for M. tuberculosis, confirming the diagnostic hypothesis of cutaneous TB.
